name: n8n

auth.keyHelp: In n8n open Settings > n8n API, choose Create an API key, set a label and expiry (on Enterprise pick only the list and read scopes), and copy the key.

notes: Runs on the user own host or on n8n Cloud, so URLs use {site}. Base URL: self-hosted is <host>:<port>/<N8N_PATH>/api/v1 (a custom path prefix is possible; put it in the site address), Cloud is https://<name>.app.n8n.cloud/api/v1. The key goes in the X-N8N-API-KEY header with no prefix. The API is not available during the free trial; it is on Cloud Starter, Pro and Enterprise and all self-hosted editions. Create the key at Settings > n8n API > Create an API key; the docs give no URL path for that page, so keyUrl is just {site}. NO READ-ONLY KEY unless Enterprise: only Enterprise instances can limit a key with scopes (for example workflow:list, workflow:read, execution:list, execution:read, tag:list, tag:read); on any other plan the key has full access to the account, so treat it as full access. The docs describe no read-only toggle; picking only list and read scopes approximates one. Scope names read from the authentication page: workflow:list, workflow:read, workflow:activate (covers activate and deactivate), execution:list, execution:read, execution:retry, tag:list. The test call is GET /workflows?limit=1 (needs workflow:list on a scoped key) and the API names no whoami endpoint, so who is null; the user endpoints (GET /users) are restricted to the instance owner and so are not used. Pagination: default page size 100, maximum 250 through limit, and a nextCursor value in the response is passed back as cursor. POST calls accept an Idempotency-Key header. Endpoints read from the OpenAPI embedded in the docs: GET /workflows, GET /workflows/{workflowId}, POST /workflows/{workflowId}/activate and /deactivate (also publish and unpublish), GET /executions (filters status, workflowId, projectId, includeData, startedAfter, startedBefore), GET /executions/{executionId}, POST /executions/{executionId}/retry and /stop, and GET /tags. The API playground is only on self-hosted n8n. Official MCP: n8n has a built-in instance-level MCP server on every instance (and Cloud). Enable it as an owner or admin at Settings > Instance-level MCP; the Server URL is copied from the Connect a client dialog and ends in /mcp-server/http, so {site}/mcp-server/http is my reading of that and the exact prefix is not printed. Two auth methods: OAuth (recommended) or an API key tab where n8n generates a separate personal access token for MCP, sent as Authorization: Bearer; that MCP token is not the same as the REST API key. Per-client setup steps need n8n 2.33.0 or newer. It exposes only workflows the user individually enabled for MCP (search_workflows can see every workflow the user may view, preview only), and from 2.13.0 it can build and edit workflows and data tables. A separate MCP Server Trigger node makes a single workflow its own MCP server, which is a different thing.
